output:
**Tracked dumper – buying instead of hiring**

Lee,

I know you’ll want to see the numbers before agreeing to anything, so here it is written down. We’ve known each other 15 years and done enough of these jobs to know when we’re wasting time and money.

**What hiring is costing us**

We’ve hired the tracked dumper for 14 days this year from the place in Sittingbourne. At £85 a day, plus £30 delivery each time, that’s roughly **£1,600 all in**.

It’s not just the money either. In September they didn’t have one available, so we ended up barrowing six ton of muck at the Hernhill job. That added two extra days and your back was gone for a week. Another time the delivery driver didn’t turn up until 11 and we lost half the morning waiting around.

**The one I’ve found**

There’s a bloke in Faversham selling a **2019 500kg tracked dumper for £1,650 ono**. He says it had new tracks fitted last spring. Going halves would be **£825 each**, and it can live under cover in my lean-to at the yard.

We’ve already got three patio digs and the Boughton drive booked in for spring, so it’s not something we’d be buying on the off-chance we might use it.

At this year’s level of use, the purchase price would be covered by what we’d otherwise spend on hire in about a year. At half that use, it’s roughly two years. That’s before servicing and repairs, so there will still be some ongoing cost, but we wouldn’t be paying out £1,600 a year on hire.

I suggest we split servicing **50/50**, and whoever breaks it pays for the repair. If we buy it and it doesn’t work out for us, we can sell it on. These dumpers hold their value, so it isn’t money we’d necessarily lose.

Come and have a look at it with me **this Saturday**. It’s worth going before somebody else has it. If it’s rough or we don’t like the look of it once we’re there, we walk away.
